transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-14
Time: 09:30 PT
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Monica Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Peregrine Head of Security), Marcus Hale (Platform Engineer), Priya Singh (Compliance)

Summary:
Redwood team walked through the admin event capture surface, what events are instrumented today, export options (batch S3 export, streaming Firehose/Kinesis, webhook push), retention tiers, and customer-managed key options for at-rest encryption. Customer wanted clarity on what is captured for admin activity vs. inference telemetry, options for offsite archive, and how deletion/retention controls work for legal hold scenarios.

Topics: audit event schema, admin console events, token/key rotations, KMS CMEK support, SSO/RBAC audit trails, export formats, retention and legal hold, SOC2/ISO implications, metrics vs. events, cost for long-term archival.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. I'm Jordan from Redwood. Monica's on the call to run through the technical bits. Lena, Marcus, Priya — thanks for joining. Quick context: this is a deep dive on admin events and export playbooks for Peregrine's compliance program.

[00:16] Lena: Hi all. Yeah, we've got a few regs to satisfy and want to validate what you capture natively and what we'll need to export and keep in our systems. SOC two obviously, and some regional residency needs.

[00:28] Monica: Great. I'll start with an overview then show examples. We instrument three broad categories: control-plane admin events, data-plane inference metadata, and platform telemetry. For compliance you probably care most about control-plane events — user logins, token creates/deletes, role changes, permission grants, audit export ops, KMS key usage.

[00:46] Marcus: When you say token creates, is that service tokens only or API keys issued via console too?

[00:52] Monica: Both. We capture console sessions (SSO events) and API key lifecycle events. The event payload includes actor, timestamp, IP, originating region, event type, and object id. Sometimes the transcript picks up "R-Dedicated" as "Red Wood Dedicated" — sorry, that's a common ASR quirk in our exports.

[01:12] Priya: Can you show an actual event example? For our auditors we need field names.

[01:18] Monica: Yep. Example snippet: {"event_type":"api_key.create","actor":{"id":"u-123","email":"lena@peregrine.com"},"timestamp":"2025-11-14T16:18:07Z","ip":"18.42.1.23","region":"us-west-2","resource":{"id":"ak-9f8","type":"api_key"},"outcome":"success"}. We'll share a full gzipped ndjson sample after. Note: beach of transcription — sometimes we show KMS as "K-M-S" in exports but the actual field is "encryption.kms_key_id".

[01:48] Lena: That looks good. What about console admin actions — role changes and policy edits? We need full before and after diff for certain events.

[01:56] Monica: We do include deltas for config-change events where possible. For example role.assign will contain previous and updated role arrays if the change is via console or API. If a change is performed by an automated system it's recorded with the integration id. There are limits: we don't store full historical large blobs indefinitely in the hot store — for giant policy docs we store a hash and a snapshot to the export bucket on change.

[02:24] Marcus: About exports — what's immediate vs batched? We don't want >1 hour delay for admin events because auditors complain.

[02:31] Monica: Two export modes: streaming and batch. Streaming exports via Firehose/Kinesis or webhook get events within seconds (typical tail-latency < 5s). Batch S3 exports are configurable (hourly/daily) and are gzipped newline-delimited JSON. For legal/forensic use we usually recommend streaming + daily S3 snapshots for durable archive.

[02:58] Priya: Are exports encrypted with customer-managed keys? Our policy requires customer control over encryption keys for long term archive.

[03:06] Jordan: Yes. We support CMEK for S3 exports and for storage at rest in Private deployments. For hosted exports, you can provide a KMS key in your account and we will use it to encrypt the object prior to handoff. For Dedicated/Private there's an option to bring-your-own-HSM via KMIP integrations, though that needs extra onboarding.

[03:30] Lena: HSM support — is that for on-prem only? We run an HSM for signing tokens and would like keys never to leave our control.

[03:37] Monica: HSM-backed key wrapping is supported in Private deployments where the control plane can be configured to not persist plaintext keys. For hosted, we do CMEK where the encrypted blob is handed off but key usage is logged. If you need zero key exposure, Private with HSM is the recommended path.

[03:56] Marcus: How do you handle data residency? If we request that logs remain in eu-west-1, is that possible?

[04:02] Monica: Yes — routing policies allow audit exports to be region-anchored. For hosted customers we can pin export buckets to a region and ensure processing happens in-region. Private deployments naturally keep everything in-customer region.

[04:18] Lena: A quick question on RBAC/SSO — do you capture SAML assertions or just metadata about the login? Auditors often want SSO timestamps and assertion id.

[04:27] Monica: We capture assertion id, timestamp, issuer, subject and the MFA outcome — not the full assertion body. We avoid storing full assertion payloads to reduce PII surface. You can configure to include more fields in exports if necessary under a special agreement.

[04:46] Priya: For retention, our policy is segregated: 90 days for analyst access, 7 years for compliance sealed archive. Can you support multi-tier retention?

[04:56] Jordan: Yes. We have retention tiers: default hot retention on platform (30/90/180 days based on plan) and then archival to your S3 for long-term (you control lifecycle to Glacier). There's also an optional Redwood-managed cold archive add-on where we retain compressed archives for you for a configured period. Cost implications discussed later in the quote.

[05:18] Marcus: If we request deletion (subject access request or legal purge), how are exports handled? If we purge a user, do we redact old events or only future ones?

[05:28] Monica: Good question. Deletion on the platform removes user identifiers from hot storage and future events reference anonymized ids. For exported archives — once events are handed off to your bucket we don't control downstream deletion. For legal purge we'd coordinate a delivered manifest marking events to delete and provide guidance. For our managed archives we can perform redaction on request but it'll require a runbook and proofing process.

[05:52] Lena: For SOC two audits, auditors want evidence of KMS rotation and key access. Are those events captured?

[05:58] Monica: Yes. Key rotation, KMS decrypt requests and key grants are logged. The event includes actor, request parameters, and outcome. We also surface a key-usage report that maps service principal usage to timestamps.

[06:14] Jordan: A note on fidelity — sometimes ASR in our meeting exports messes up product names (we see "KV cash" instead of "KV cache"), but the actual event fields are consistent JSON keys. We'll send a clean sample file so auditors see canonical fields.

[06:29] Marcus: For streaming to our Firehose — can we use VPC endpoints and private link? We don't want traffic going over the public internet.

[06:36] Monica: Absolutely. We support VPC endpoints and AWS PrivateLink for streaming. For private deployments it's all internal. For hosted streaming we establish a mutual TLS connection to your endpoint and we can route via PrivateLink where available.

[06:54] Priya: About format — is it newline-delimited JSON; do you include schema versions?

[07:00] Monica: Yes, ndjson gzipped for batch exports. Every event carries a schema_version field so you can handle upgrades. We also sign each batch manifest with an HMAC and include a manifest.json with file checksums and schema version.

[07:18] Lena: Do you offer a push-based webhook for critical alerts? Like immediate push on admin.role.grant so our SIEM ingests in real time?

[07:25] Monica: Yep — webhooks for critical event types are supported, with retry/backoff and a configurable severity filter. Webhooks are signed. For high-throughput we recommend Firehose streaming.

[07:40] Marcus: How granular are events for model changes? We change model configs often and need to know who changed temperature/quantization or pinned a version.

[07:47] Monica: Model-config-change events include the parameter diffs and the user. For heavyweight objects we store a snapshot to the export bucket and include a pointer. We also capture rollout events (canary start, canary end, rollback) with timestamps and traffic percentages.

[08:05] Priya: Anything special for private deployments with respect to audit collection?

[08:10] Monica: Private deployments have local log collectors, and we can configure direct streaming to your SIEM without leaving the customer network. We also support FIPS endpoints and can disable any telemetry that isn't required for your compliance posture.

[08:26] Jordan: We should talk costs briefly — long-term archival to your S3 is standard S3 costs. Redwood-managed cold archive and additional retention beyond plan come with a monthly fee. We'll put pricing in the follow-up.

[08:37] Lena: Competitors — we looked at BigCloudAI and EdgeServe; can you summarize differences on audit/retention?

[08:45] Jordan: High-level: BigCloudAI offers native export but their CMEK integration is limited to certain tiers; EdgeServe has strong on-prem story but heavier ops. Redwood focuses on consistent exports across hosted/dedicated/private with baked-in schema versioning and rollout/event diffs. We'll send a one-pager.

[09:02] Marcus: A quick technical: do you store plaintext policy blobs in the event store? You mentioned hashes plus snapshots. How easy is it to retrieve the snapshot?

[09:10] Monica: Snapshots are written to export bucket with a deterministic key so you'll be able to fetch them. The event references the snapshot key. For security we recommend snapshot encryption with your KMS key.

[09:22] Priya: What about tamper evidence? Auditors often want a chain of custody with checksums and immutability hints.

[09:29] Monica: We include manifest checksums and HMACs for each batch. For higher assurance, we can bake event digests into an append-only journal and provide audit proofs on request — that's part of our compliance package.

[09:46] Lena: If we want the longest retention with regional residency and HSM, sounds like Private is the path. But we'd like to pilot streaming from hosted first. Is that realistic?

[09:55] Jordan: Yes, pilot hosted streaming with CMEK to your S3 + Firehose is common. Then if you need stronger guarantees or no key exposure, move to Private.

[10:04] Marcus: For our pilot, we want the following events: api_key.*, user.login, role.*, kms.*, model.config_change, rollout.*, admin.export.*. Can you filter at source?

[10:12] Monica: Yes — you can subscribe to event categories and severity. For the pilot we'll enable the list you provided and send both streaming and hourly batch to your bucket. We'll include manifest files and schema docs.

[10:27] Jordan: Quick recap of next steps: Monica will share sample ndjson and manifest, Jordan will send KMS whitepaper and pricing, Marcus will send the list of must-retain event types and legal requirements. We'll aim to start pilot week of 11/24.

[10:41] Lena: Sounds good. One final question — do you retain admin exports in any control-plane logs that Redwood employees can access? We need assurance of admin access controls and VSM.

[10:51] Monica: We have internal RBAC for access to export logs. Access is audited and subject to least-privilege. For shared hosted accounts we run a separation-of-duties review. We can provide an access list and SOC2 evidence in the pack.

[11:04] Priya: Perfect. That's all from my side. Thanks.

[11:08] Jordan: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts.

End of meeting.

Artifacts mentioned:
- Sample ndjson gzipped export (to be uploaded)
- KMS whitepaper and SOC2 checklist (Jordan)
- Pricing for archival and Dedicated retention add-on (Jordan)
- Pilot configuration doc and event subscription manifest (Monica)

Notes on transcription artifacts: occasional ASR errors (e.g., "Red Wood" for Redwood, "KV cash" for KV cache), product names may be split like "Red wood Dedicated". We'll attach canonical event samples in follow-up to avoid confusion.
